posts.title: Invisalign vs Braces: Which Is Right for You?
posts.author: Dr. Meera Krishnan
posts.excerpt: Both straighten teeth. They do it on different timelines, at different costs, and they ask different things of you.
body: The honest answer is that the better option depends on how much movement your teeth need and how disciplined you are about wearing a tray for twenty-two hours a day.

Aligners are removable, nearly invisible and far kinder to your gums during cleaning. They handle mild to moderate crowding, spacing and mild bite corrections extremely well. What they cannot do easily is rotate a stubborn premolar or close a large extraction space.

Fixed braces stay on the teeth, which removes compliance from the equation entirely. For teenagers, complex bites, and large corrections, they remain faster and more predictable. Ceramic brackets soften the visual impact if that is the concern.

Cost sits in a similar band for comparable cases in Bangalore, though aligner cases with more trays climb higher. The decision is best made after a cephalometric analysis rather than from a price list.

posts.title: How to Take Care of Your Dental Implants
posts.author: Dr. Kabir Shah
posts.excerpt: An implant cannot decay, but the bone holding it can be lost. Maintenance is the whole game.
body: Implants fail for one reason far more often than any other: peri-implantitis, an inflammatory loss of the bone around the fixture. It is caused by plaque, and it is preventable.

Brush twice daily with a soft brush, and clean between the implant and its neighbours every single day with an interdental brush sized to the gap. Floss alone often skims past the wider implant emergence profile.
Avoid using the implant crown as a tool. Opening packaging, cracking shells or chewing ice concentrates force in a way natural ligament-supported teeth would absorb but implants cannot.
Book a professional maintenance visit every six months. We use titanium-safe instruments and check the bone level radiographically once a year.

posts.title: Teeth Whitening: Myths vs Facts
posts.author: Dr. Aanya Mehta
posts.excerpt: Charcoal, lemon juice and baking soda are not whitening agents. Here is what actually changes tooth shade.
body: Whitening works by allowing peroxide to diffuse through enamel and break the double bonds in stain molecules within the dentine. Anything that does not do this is polishing at best and abrasion at worst.
Charcoal powders are abrasive. They remove surface stain and, over months, enamel with it. The teeth then look darker, because the yellower dentine underneath begins to show through.
Sensitivity during professional whitening is common, temporary and manageable with a potassium nitrate desensitiser. It is not a sign of damage.
Existing crowns, veneers and composite fillings will not change shade. If you plan to whiten, whiten first and match the restorations afterwards.

posts.title: Kids Dental Care: Tips for Healthy Smiles
posts.author: Dr. Aanya Mehta
posts.excerpt: The first dental visit should happen by the first birthday, and it should be boring on purpose.
body: Bring your child in for a first visit around their first birthday, before anything hurts. The point of that appointment is familiarity, not treatment. A child who has sat in the chair happily three times will cooperate when something actually needs doing.
Brush for them until they can tie their own shoelaces. Fine motor control simply is not there before that, no matter how enthusiastic they are.
Use a smear of fluoridated toothpaste under three, and a pea-sized amount after. Spit, do not rinse, so the fluoride stays in contact with the enamel.
Milk teeth matter. They hold space for the permanent teeth behind them, and losing one early to decay is a common cause of crowding later.

posts.title: What Really Causes Sensitive Teeth
posts.author: Dr. Rahul Menon
posts.excerpt: Cold water on one tooth is a different problem from cold water on all of them. The distinction matters.
body: Generalised sensitivity across many teeth usually points to exposed dentine at the gum line, from aggressive brushing, acidic diet or gum recession. It responds well to a desensitising paste and a change in technique.
Sharp sensitivity in one tooth that lingers after the stimulus is removed is a different signal. That often indicates irreversible pulpitis, and it needs a radiograph rather than a new toothpaste.
Grinding at night thickens the muscles and cracks enamel over time, producing sensitivity that is worse on waking. A night guard usually resolves it.
If pain wakes you at night or throbs without provocation, treat it as urgent rather than waiting for your next routine visit.

posts.title: Your First Visit: What Actually Happens
posts.author: Demo Dental Team
posts.excerpt: A walkthrough of the first forty-five minutes, so nothing in the appointment is a surprise.
body: You will spend the first ten minutes talking, not being treated. We take a medical history, ask what brought you in, and note any medication that affects bleeding or healing.
A full examination follows: each tooth charted, gum pockets measured, and an OPG radiograph if you have not had one in the past year.
You then see your own images on the screen while we explain what we found, what is urgent, what can wait, and what it will cost. Nothing is booked before you agree to it.
Most first visits end with a scaling and polish if the gums allow it, so you leave with something done rather than only a plan.
